question: In light of the incident involving New Democracy MEP Anna-Michelle Asimakopoulou, who was forced to withdraw from the New Democracy candidate list for the European elections in June, the resignation of the Interior Ministry Secretary-General Michalis Stavrianoudakis and the dismissal of New Democracy’s Secretary for Diaspora Affairs Nikos Theodoropoulos, can the Commission answer the following: 1.

What steps will it take to stop governmental actors, who were clearly acting in the interests of their party and in breach of Articles 6(1)(a) and 7(1) of the GDPR, from breaching the personal data of Greek voters living overseas?1

How could the Commission contribute to a fair election process in light of the mass breach of personal data by a government that was condemned, in a European Parliament resolution adopted in February, for undermining the rule of law, bearing in mind that the breach harms electoral competition and undermines fair elections?2

How will it safeguard the integrity of the investigation currently being conducted by the Greek Data Protection Authority against any interference from the government, bearing in mind that the latter is conducting its own parallel investigation and is already arriving at its own conclusions?3
answer: EN on behalf of the European Commission (19.7.2024) Member States have a primary responsibility to monitor the application of Regulation (EU) 2016/679 on General Data Protection (GDPR)1 and to take the necessary steps for enforcement.

Enforcement of the GDPR lies with the EU-27 independent national data protection authorities and courts, who investigate complaints, provide advice on data protection issues and determine when the GDPR has been breached, without prejudice to the Commission’s role as guardian of the Treaties. The Commission understands that the Greek data protection authority has launched an investigation into this matter.
As a general rule, the Commission does not comment on ongoing investigations. The European Data Protection Board is responsible to ensure consistent application of the GDPR.

In the run up to 2019 European Parliament elections, it issued a statement on the use of personal data in the course of political campaigns2, which complements the Commission guidance on the application of EU data protection law in the electoral context3.

The Commission Recommendation on inclusive and resilient elections 2023/2829, issued as part of the Defence of Democracy package4 on December 2023, acknowledges particular and far-reaching Member States’ responsibilities to foster broad and inclusive democratic participation and to promote free, fair and resilient elections in the EU.

The Commission works closely with all Member States’ competent authorities to promote free and fair elections in the EU and support the exchange of best practices on elections, including in the framework of the European Cooperation Network on Elections5.
1 Regulation (EU) 2016/679 of the European Parliament and of the Council of 27 April 2016 on the protection

of natural persons with regard to the processing of personal data and on the free movement of such data, and repealing Directive 95/46/EC (General Data Protection Regulation), OJ L 119, 4.5.2016, p. 1–88. 2 Statement 2/2019 on the use of personal data in the course of political campaigns: https://www.edpb.europa.eu/sites/default/files/files/file1/edpb-2019-03-13-statement-on-elections_en.pdf 3 COM(2018) 638 final.
